name: Dalfon
title: Son of Haman
summary: Dalfon was one of the ten sons of Haman, the Agagite, who was an enemy of the Jewish people in the Persian Empire. He was killed along with his brothers when the Jews defended themselves against their enemies, as described in the book of Esther. His death marked God's protection of His people from destruction.

keyEvents.title: Haman's Plan to Destroy the Jews
keyEvents.description: Haman, the father of Dalphon, planned to destroy all the Jews in the Persian Empire after Mordecai refused to bow down to him.

keyEvents.title: Dalphon Mentioned as One of Haman's Sons
keyEvents.description: Dalphon is mentioned as the second of Haman's ten sons in the book of Esther.

keyEvents.title: The Jews' Victory Over Their Enemies
keyEvents.description: When the Jews defended themselves against their enemies on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, Haman's ten sons, including Dalphon, were killed in the fortress of Susa.

keyEvents.title: Queen Esther Requests That Haman's Sons Be Hanged
keyEvents.description: Queen Esther asked King Ahasuerus to have the bodies of Haman's ten sons hung on poles as a public demonstration of justice.

keyEvents.title: The Festival of Purim Is Established
keyEvents.description: The killing of Haman and his sons, including Dalphon, was remembered through the establishment of the festival of Purim, which Jews celebrate in memory of their deliverance.
